1. `if (size_t(end - it) >= 8)` - enters the fast path
2. It scans for quotes using 8-byte chunks

The `memcpy(p, start, 8)` copies 8 bytes from `start` into `p`. Since `start` can be up to `it - 1` (before the quote), and `p` can be up to `n` bytes in, the copy of 8 bytes from `start` could read past `it` (the quote position) but that's within the input buffer since `available_padding >= 8`.

If `start` is near the end of the input buffer, this could read past the end. Actually wait - `available_padding = size_t(end - it)` where `it` points to the quote. So `end - it` is the bytes after the quote. If `available_padding >= 8`, then there are at least 8 bytes after the quote. But `start` can be at most `it - 1` (since `start < it` in the loop).
